mainTopic: Setting and uprooting a וסת: רב and שמואל on the skipping cycle, and רב פפא's rules on one or two sightings
overview: A woman saw blood on the 15th, 16th and 17th of three months in a row. רב says she has set a skipping וסת. שמואל says she needs three skips. The גמרא shows that both agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that a pattern needs three times. They only disagree about whether the first sighting, on the 15th, counts. A ברייתא about a woman used to the 15th challenges רב, and he answers that a woman with an old fixed day is different. Another ברייתא, about the 21st, 22nd and 23rd, challenges שמואל. He answers that she was used to the 20th, and the ברייתא's wording supports him. Then רב פפא explains two lines of the משנה. One sighting already brings a worry, even outside her days of נדה. A pattern seen only twice is uprooted by a single change, and a ברייתא about days twenty and thirty supports this.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about a skipping cycle
steps.stepSummary: A woman saw blood on the 15th, then the 16th, then the 17th of three months in a row. רב says she has set a skipping וסת. שמואל says she must skip three times first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: a woman saw blood on the 15th of one month, the 16th of the next month, and the 17th of the month after that. רב says she has set a וסת by skipping. שמואל says she has not set it until she skips three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a dispute between רב and שמואל about a woman whose period moves one day later each month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three sightings here, but only two skips: from 15 to 16, and from 16 to 17. רב thinks this is already enough for a fixed skipping pattern. שמואל wants three actual skips, which would mean seeing on the 15th, 16th, 17th and 18th.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's set, predictable cycle for seeing blood
Skipping: the date moves forward by a set amount each time

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'לחדש זה' are repeated three times, but they do not mean the same month. Each one means the next month in the sequence: the 15th of month one, the 16th of month two, and the 17th of month three.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רָאֲתָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר לְחֹדֶשׁ זֶה,
phrases.english: She saw blood on the fifteenth of this month,
and on the sixteenth of the next month,
and on the seventeenth of the month after that —

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: קָבְעָה לָהּ וֶסֶת לְדִילּוּג,
phrases.english: Rav says: She has set for herself a cycle by skipping,
and Shmuel says: Not until she skips three times.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רָאֲתָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר לְחֹדֶשׁ זֶה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: 15, 16, 17 sets a skipping וסת. שמואל: three actual skips are needed.

steps.title: Is this the same as the dispute about marrying after husbands died?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל are repeating the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. That dispute is about a woman whose husbands died: does a pattern need two times or three?
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב and שמואל disagree on the same point as רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? A ברייתא teaches: a woman married a first husband and he died, then a second and he died. She may not marry a third, says רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she may marry a third, but not a fourth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to link the רב and שמואל dispute to an older dispute about how many times something must happen to count as a pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי sets a pattern after two times. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sets it only after three. The suggestion is that רב sides with רבי and שמואל sides with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא tests)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav and Shmuel

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי וְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָמִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: disagree in the dispute of Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?
As it is taught: She married a first husband and he died,
a second and he died —
she may not marry a third; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
She may marry a third, but she may not marry a fourth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the רב and שמואל dispute as the same as an earlier תנאים dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the root of the רב and שמואל dispute whether a pattern needs two times or three?

steps.title: No: everyone needs three; the question is whether the 15th counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the link. Both רב and שמואל agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that a pattern needs three times. They disagree only about whether the first sighting, on the 15th, counts as one of the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. Here they disagree about this: רב holds that the 15th is part of the count. שמואל holds that since she did not see on the 15th as a result of a skip, it is not part of the count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggestion and finds a different, narrower reason for the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the 15th starts the chain, so 15, 16 and 17 give three sightings in the pattern. For שמואל, only a sighting that came after a skip counts. The 15th was not reached by skipping, so only the 16th and 17th count, and she needs one more.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל require three times, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does. The only question is whether the opening sighting, before any skip, counts as one of the three.

phrases.aramaic: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: No, everyone agrees with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and here they disagree about this:
Rav holds that the fifteenth is part of the count,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בְּדִילּוּג חֲזֵיתֵיהּ —
phrases.english: and Shmuel holds that since she did not see it by skipping —
phrases.notes: He means she did not reach the 15th by moving a day forward from the 14th of the month before.

phrases.english: it is not part of the count.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects tying רב to רבי. Everyone holds that three times are needed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute is not about how many times are needed. It is about whether the first sighting, which came before any skip, counts toward the three.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the same 15-16-17 case challenges רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought against רב. A woman used to seeing on the 15th changed to the 16th, then to the 17th. The ruling is that the 16th becomes permitted, while the 15th and 17th are forbidden. It does not treat her as having a fixed skipping cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: if she was used to seeing on the 15th and changed to the 16th, both days are forbidden. If she then changed to the 17th, the 16th becomes permitted, and the 15th and 17th are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as an objection to רב. It is setting up the challenge, which the גמרא will spell out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 15th stays forbidden because it was her old fixed day. The 17th is forbidden because she just saw on it. The 16th, a single time that did not repeat, is now permitted. The ברייתא never says she has set a skipping וסת from the 15th, 16th and 17th. That seems to go against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to; accustomed (to seeing on a certain day)
Forbidden (to be with her husband on those days)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden' here does not mean she is טמאה. It means that on that day she must keep away from her husband, because she might see blood.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: If she was accustomed to see blood on the fifteenth day,
and she changed to the sixteenth day —
both this day and that day are forbidden.
If she then changed to the seventeenth day —
the sixteenth becomes permitted,
and the fifteenth and seventeenth are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the dispute has been explained, a source is brought against רב's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב, who says that 15, 16, 17 sets a skipping וסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes the exact 15, 16, 17 sequence. Its rulings name only the 15th and 17th as forbidden and never mention a skipping pattern. This suggests no skipping וסת was set, against רב.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: only the eighteenth sets the pattern
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that when she moved again to the 18th, a pattern is finally set. This is a challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she changed again to the eighteenth day, all the earlier days become permitted. From now on she is forbidden only from the eighteenth onward. This is difficult for רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 4 and states clearly that it is a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the skipping pattern is set only on the 16th, 17th and 18th, which is three moves away from the 15th. רב had said that 15, 16, 17 is already enough. So the ברייתא seems to need one more sighting than רב does.

phrases.english: If she changed to the eighteenth day,
all of them are permitted,
phrases.notes: Even the 15th, her old day, is now permitted, because she has moved away from it three times.

phrases.english: and nothing is forbidden except
from the eighteenth onward.
phrases.notes: He means the next step in her skipping pattern, so after the 18th she must watch for the 19th.

phrases.english: This is difficult for רב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 4 and states the challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a skipping וסת is set by 15, 16, 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא the pattern is set only at the 18th, which requires three skips after the 15th, and not two.

steps.title: רב answers: a woman already used to a day is different
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the ברייתא speaks about a woman who was already used to seeing on the 15th, so it is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: a woman who was used to a fixed day is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא's case is different from his own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the 15th was her old, fixed day. It belongs to the old pattern, so it cannot count as the first link of a new skipping pattern. In רב's case the 15th was not an old fixed day, so it does count as the first of the three.

phrases.english: רב can say to you:
a woman used to a fixed day is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5 by setting the ברייתא's case apart.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (שאני). The ברייתא itself says she was a למודה, so רב does not need to narrow it to a special case. He only points out why that detail matters.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that three skips past the first sighting are always needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the 15th was her old fixed day, it does not count as the start of a new pattern. When the 15th is not an old fixed day, רב's count of 15, 16, 17 still works.

steps.title: Why did the challenger bring this ברייתא at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: the ברייתא clearly speaks about a woman used to the 15th, so why did anyone use it to challenge רב?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who raised this challenge, why did he raise it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why the challenger brought this ברייתא, since its case so clearly involves an old fixed day. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens by saying she was 'used to' the 15th, so רב's answer seems obvious. The question pushes the challenger's side to show that the ברייתא has a real point beyond that obvious detail.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks; he raises a challenge

phrases.english: And the one who asked it,
phrases.notes: This means the one who brought this ברייתא as a challenge against רב.

phrases.english: why did he ask it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the challenge from Step 5 in light of רב's answer in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the challenger thought the ברייתא was teaching, given that it clearly speaks about a woman with an old fixed day.

steps.title: The ברייתא needed to teach the case of a woman with an old fixed day
steps.stepSummary: The challenger's side explains that the ברייתא mentions the old fixed day for its own reason. Without it, we might think two changes are enough to undo an old fixed day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a woman used to a fixed day was needed. You might have said: since she was used to a day and then moved away from it, two times are enough to undo it. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא mentions her old fixed day in order to teach a separate point, so the challenger could still see it as a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this reading, the ברייתא is teaching that an old fixed day is undone only after three changes, and not after two. So the detail that she was 'used to' the 15th does not prove that the 15th fails to count toward a new pattern. That is why the challenger felt he could still bring the ברייתא against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: The case of a woman used to a day was needed,
since you might have said:
since she was used to it and moved away from it,
two times are enough to undo it,
so it teaches us that it is not so.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא mentions the old fixed day to teach that it needs three changes to be undone, and not two. So the challenger could read it as a real challenge to רב.
steps.whatToRemember: An old fixed day (למודה) is undone only after three changes. For רב, the old fixed day also cannot serve as the first link of a new skipping pattern.

steps.title: A ברייתא that seems to set a pattern too quickly for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that sightings on the 21st, 22nd and 23rd of three months set a skipping וסת. That fits רב, and so it is brought as a refutation of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A challenge: If she saw on the 21st of one month, the 22nd of the next month and the 23rd of the next month, she has set a וסת. If in the third month she skipped to the 24th instead, she has not set a וסת. This is a refutation of שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to שמואל and brings a ברייתא that seems to go against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 21, 22, 23 already set the pattern, which is exactly like רב's 15, 16, 17. שמואל demanded three skips beyond the first sighting, so this ברייתא seems to refute him outright.

keyTerms.meaning: She has set a fixed cycle for herself

phrases.english: They raised a challenge:

phrases.aramaic: רָאֲתָה יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד בְּחֹדֶשׁ זֶה,
phrases.english: If she saw on the twenty-first day of this month,
the twenty-second day of that month,
and the twenty-third day of that month,
she has set a fixed cycle.
If she skipped to the twenty-fourth day,
she has not set a fixed cycle.
This is a refutation of שמואל!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רב, the גמרא now challenges שמואל with a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that she must skip three times beyond the first sighting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sets the pattern with 21, 22, 23, which are only two skips after the first sighting.

steps.title: שמואל answers: she was used to the twentieth
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the ברייתא speaks about a woman who was used to seeing on the 20th and then moved to the 21st. So 21, 22, 23 are really three skips.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל can tell you: What case are we dealing with here? A woman who was used to seeing on the 20th, and changed to the 21st.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the refutation by placing the ברייתא in a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her old fixed day was the 20th, then 21, 22 and 23 are three separate skips. That matches שמואל's demand for three skips, so the ברייתא no longer refutes him.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrow reading)

phrases.english: שמואל can say to you:
What case are we dealing with here?
Where she was used to seeing on the twentieth day,
and she changed to the twenty-first day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא (narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא sets the pattern after only two skips.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her old fixed day was the 20th, so 21, 22, 23 are three skips, as שמואל requires.
steps.confusionAlert: Both answers use an old fixed day in the same way. The old day itself is not counted, and the first move away from it (15 to 16 in רב's ברייתא, 20 to 21 here) is the first counted skip. Here that gives 21, 22, 23 as three skips.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording supports שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's choice of the 21st, instead of a round number like the 20th, shows that the 20th was her old fixed day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is precise too: why did it skip over the 20th and pick the 21st? Learn from this that the 20th was her old day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל's answer by pointing to a detail in the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא would normally start from a simple, round day like the 20th. Starting at the 21st hints that the 20th had a role of its own, as her old fixed day. That supports שמואל's reading, and the גמרא concludes 'learn from this.'

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (supports this reading)
Learn from this; that proves it

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל protect their views by pointing to an old fixed day in the ברייתא. For שמואל, the ברייתא's choice of the 21st shows that the 20th was her earlier fixed day.

phrases.english: The wording is precise as well,
for it left aside the twentieth day
and took the twenty-first day.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 10 from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's reading that the woman was used to the 20th.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא chose the 21st over the more natural 20th as its starting day.

steps.title: One sighting is enough to worry, though not to set a fixed cycle
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה's rule of three sightings is only for setting a fixed וסת. For worrying, one sighting is already enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a woman does not set a fixed cycle until she sets it (three times). רב פפא said: that is only for really setting it. But to be careful about it, even after one time she must worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about setting a וסת. Then רב פפא adds a limit to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires three sightings to make a fixed וסת. רב פפא separates two things: setting a fixed pattern, which takes three, and simply worrying about the day, which starts after just one. So after one sighting she must already keep away from her husband on that day next time.

keyTerms.meaning: for setting it as a fixed cycle
to be concerned / to worry about it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'setting' a וסת with 'worrying' about one. One sighting does not make a fixed וסת, but it already brings a worry for that day.

phrases.english: For a woman does not set a fixed cycle for herself
until she sets it, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. It means until she sees on that pattern three times.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We only said this for setting it,
but to be concerned about it
after one time she is concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְמִקְבְּעַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה after the רב and שמואל discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three sightings are needed to set a fixed וסת, but one sighting already requires concern for that day.

steps.title: Isn't this already taught in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב פפא adds, since the משנה already says a woman who changed from the 15th to the 20th must worry about both days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned: if she was used to seeing on the 15th and she changed to the 20th, both days are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא for saying something the משנה already teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case she saw on the 20th only once, yet the 20th is already forbidden. That is exactly רב פפא's point that one sighting brings a worry. So his statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us? (asking what is new here)
both this day and that day are forbidden

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned it:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: If she was used to seeing on the fifteenth day,
and she changed to the twentieth day
both this and that are forbidden!
phrases.notes: The 20th is forbidden even though she saw on it only once. That is why the גמרא thinks this already teaches רב פפא's rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's statement in step 12 as already taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's statement that one sighting already brings concern
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already forbids the 20th after a single sighting, so רב פפא adds nothing new.

steps.title: The משנה alone might have been limited to her usual period days
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone we might think the worry applies only if the new sighting came during her days of נדה. רב פפא teaches that it applies even outside those days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said: that is only when she saw during her days of נדה. But when she saw outside her days of נדה, I would say she does not need to worry. So רב פפא teaches us that she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רב פפא adds something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case of the 20th could be a sighting that came during her ימי נדה, the days when a period is normal. Then we might think a sighting during the eleven days of זיבה brings no worry. רב פפא teaches that one sighting brings a worry at any time.

keyTerms.meaning: if we had it only from there
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
her days of נדה, when a period is normal

steps.whatToRemember: A single sighting brings a worry for that day, whether or not it came during her days of נדה.

phrases.english: If only from there, I would have said:
These words apply where she stands
within her days of menstruation,
but where she does not stand
within her days of menstruation, I would say not.
He teaches us.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed because the משנה's case can be read narrowly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry after one sighting applies only to a sighting during her ימי נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry applies even to a sighting outside her ימי נדה.

steps.title: Three changes are needed only for a cycle set by three sightings
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a וסת needs three changes to uproot it only if it was set by three sightings. A pattern seen only twice is uprooted after one change.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: she is not freed from her cycle (until it is changed three times). רב פפא said: we only said this when she set it three times, so three times are needed to uproot it. But if it was seen two times, one time uproots it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about uprooting an old וסת, and רב פפא limits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an old וסת stays until she misses it three times. רב פפא says this applies only to a real fixed וסת, set by three sightings. A pattern seen only twice was never fixed, so one change is enough to remove it.

keyTerms.meaning: freed from worrying about the old cycle day

steps.whatToRemember: The number of changes needed to uproot a pattern depends on how strong the pattern was. A fixed וסת set by three sightings needs three changes. A pattern seen only twice needs one.

phrases.english: And she is not purified from the cycle, etc.
phrases.notes: Another quote from the משנה. It means she still worries about the old day until it is uprooted three times.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
We only said this
where she set it three times,
that three times are needed to uproot it,
but if it was two times
it is uprooted by one time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דִּקְבַעְתֵּיהּ תְּלָתָא זִימְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה with a second explanation by רב פפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three changes uproot only a וסת set by three sightings. A pattern seen only twice is uprooted after one change.

steps.title: Isn't רב פפא's rule already in the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב פפא adds, since the משנה already says a וסת is only set after three sightings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רב פפא teaching us? We already learned in the משנה that a woman does not set a fixed וסת until she sets it three times!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's rule from Step 15. It says the משנה already seems to teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a pattern only becomes a fixed וסת after three sightings. So a pattern seen twice is not fixed at all, and it seems obvious that one change uproots it. The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say this.

keyTerms.meaning: to set a fixed monthly pattern

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: "He" is רב פפא, whose rule was in the step just before this one.

phrases.english: We already learned it:
A woman does not set for herself a fixed cycle
until she sets it three times!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's rule in Step 15 as already taught in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that a pattern seen twice is uprooted after one change
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a pattern needs three sightings to be fixed, a two-time pattern was never fixed. So it is obvious that one change ends it.

steps.title: We might have thought each sighting needs a matching change
steps.stepSummary: Without רב פפא we might think one sighting is uprooted by one change, two by two, and three by three. He teaches that anything less than three is uprooted by one change.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: one change uproots a pattern seen once, two changes uproot a pattern seen twice, and three uproot a pattern seen three times. So רב פפא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing a mistake we could have made without רב פפא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches when a וסת becomes fixed, but not how many changes are needed to uproot a weaker pattern. We might have matched the number of changes to the number of sightings. רב פפא teaches that only a full three-time וסת needs three changes. Anything less is uprooted by one.
steps.whatToRemember: Only a וסת set by three sightings needs three changes to uproot it. A pattern seen once or twice is uprooted by one change.

phrases.english: You might have said:
one change for a pattern seen one time,
two changes for a pattern seen two times,
and three changes for a pattern seen three times,
so he teaches us that this is not so.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a possible mistake (הוה אמינא) that the rule comes to rule out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number of changes needed to uproot a pattern matches the number of times it was seen.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a fixed three-time וסת needs three changes. One or two sightings are uprooted by a single change.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a woman who switched from day twenty to day thirty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought in line with רב פפא. If she used to see on day twenty and switched to day thirty, both days are forbidden. If day twenty passes with no sighting, she is permitted until day thirty and worries about day thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב פפא: If a woman was used to seeing blood on day twenty and changed to day thirty, both days are forbidden. If day twenty came and she did not see, she may be with her husband until day thirty, and she must worry about day thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב פפא. This first part sets up the case, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her old fixed day (twenty) still stands, and the new day (thirty) must also be worried about after just one sighting. This first part only sets up the case. The real support for רב פפא's rule from Step 15 comes in the next step, when day thirty, seen only twice, is uprooted by a single miss.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה לְמוּדָה לִהְיוֹת רוֹאָה יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים,
phrases.english: If she was used to seeing blood on day twenty,
phrases.notes: Day twenty counted from her last period.

phrases.english: and she changed and saw on day thirty
both this day and that day are forbidden.
If day twenty came and she did not see
she is permitted to be with her husband until day thirty,
and she must worry about day thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב פפא's rules.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule (Step 15) that a pattern seen only twice is uprooted by one change
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a woman who switched from day twenty to day thirty

steps.title: Day thirty becomes permitted after one miss
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. She saw on day thirty again, then missed day twenty, missed day thirty, and saw on day twenty. Day thirty becomes permitted, because a pattern seen only twice is uprooted by one change.
steps.simpleTranslation: If day thirty came and she saw, then day twenty came and she did not see, then day thirty came and she did not see, and then day twenty came and she saw, day thirty becomes permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part of the ברייתא that proves רב פפא's rule from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day thirty was seen only twice, so it never became a fixed וסת. One time where it did not come is enough to uproot it, and day thirty is permitted again. That is exactly רב פפא's rule that a two-time pattern is uprooted by one change.
steps.confusionAlert: Day thirty is not permitted because she went back to day twenty. It is permitted because day thirty was seen only twice, so missing it once is enough to uproot it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives real support from a ברייתא for רב פפא's rule that only a three-time וסת needs three changes to be uprooted.

phrases.english: If day thirty came and she saw,
then day twenty came and she did not see,
and day thirty came and she did not see,
and day twenty came and she saw,
day thirty becomes permitted,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 18 with the case that proves רב פפא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that a pattern seen twice is uprooted by one change
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that day thirty, seen only twice, becomes permitted after one miss
